chunks: And with this chain of transmission from al-Isba' ibn Nubatah, he said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'As for what follows, then concern for the world does not increase what is destined, and in it is a waste of effort; and turning to the Hereafter does not decrease from what is possible, and in it is securing the Return.' And he recited: (If it were in a rock in the sea, firm, hard, solid, smooth on its sides) (Sustenance for a soul that Allah sees; it will split from it and bring to him all that is in it) (Or if it were between the seven layers, his junction) (Allah will ease for him the ascents of its stairs) (Until he meets that which is written for him in the Tablet; if it comes to him, otherwise he goes to it). The compiler of this book said: Everything that Allah, the Mighty and High, enabled us to benefit from and did not make for anyone else that we were prevented from, we have been given sustenance and made it our sustenance; and everything that Allah, the Mighty and High, did not enable us to benefit from and made for others that we were prevented from, we have not been given sustenance and it was not made our sustenance.
ai.seo_question: How does focusing on the Hereafter affect one's pre-destined sustenance according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) elucidates the principle of *al-Rizq* (sustenance) as a fixed divine decree, teaching that worldly anxiety is futile because it neither increases one's allotted share nor diminishes capacity, whereas focusing on the Hereafter the Hereafter secures the ultimate return. The accompanying poetry emphasizes that sustenance reaches the soul regardless of physical location, reinforcing the Shia scholarly view that *Rizq* is defined by divine accessibility rather than mere human possession. This hadith serves as a cornerstone for understanding the balance between *Tawakkul* (trust in God) and active effort (*Tadbir*) within the framework of Divine Decree.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 15. And with the same chain of transmission on the authority of al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah that

The Commander of the Faithful (AS) said: “Verily, concern about this world does not increase one’s gain, and that is a waste of effort. Verily, the arrival of the Hereafter does not decrease for what it estimated in (that is) the achievement of the Return.” He composed this: If in a stable rock in the ocean, Hard and solid, gathered with smooth sides, There is sustenance for a soul that Allah sees; it will split From it and brings to him all that is in it. Or if there was between the seven layers (of heavens) his junction Allah will ease its elevation in the difficult ascent, Until he takes that which is written for him in the guarded-tablet, The soul finds sustenance; otherwise sustenance will seek it out. The Compiler of this book says: Our sustenance includes everything which Allah, the Mighty and High, has made for our benefits, and which He has made accessible to us. Our sustenance does not extend to that which Allah, the Mighty and High, has made inaccessible for us.
